items.summary: CRO disposition: retain no new proposal or queue admission this cycle. Delivery is saturated at 10/10 slots, 57 improvements remain in measurement, 21 implementation requests failed, and revenue evidence is limited to $4.92 aggregate unattributed commission for 2026-09-21. Site revenue, ROI, margin, and causal lift remain unknown. Preserve the existing allthingsmasonic.com CTA refinement as the next reversible revenue experiment after CTO releases capacity; do not create a duplicate request. Its evidence-backed hypothesis is that clearer affiliate CTA hierarchy, adjacent disclosure, and accessible responsive treatment can improve affiliate-click rate without changing destinations, tracking IDs, dependencies, or data collection. Baseline: 61 site-attributed Amazon clicks, 0 ordered items, and $0 site-attributed commission for the available window. Measure affiliate clicks, page engagement, and available site-attributed outcomes for 14 days or 100 relevant new impressions/clicks; report inconclusive if traffic is insufficient. Smallest reversible prototype is the already-queued single-surface CTA refinement with deterministic tests, build/link validation, disclosure/compliance checks, keyboard and accessibility checks, and single-diff rollback.

CRO product opportunity: treat the canonical work-lifecycle and AI-cost controls as a future control-plane product, not a new implementation this cycle. Evidence includes 108 approved proposals without execution requests, 216 stranded work items, 43 deployed improvements awaiting measurement, 21 failed implementation requests, and $1,002.46 recorded AI usage cost for September across 39 instrumented sites. Smallest reversible prototype after capacity recovery: a read-only operator scorecard joining proposal-to-request conversion, active-slot utilization, stranded-work age, failed-request repair time, measurement completion, and AI cost per site using existing telemetry only. Expected metric: improved proposal-to-request execution rate and reduced stranded-work count without increasing duplicate work. Time-to-learn: one reporting cycle after implementation. Risks: incomplete operational sweeps, partial revenue attribution, and attribution or causality overclaiming; preserve unknowns and require CTO/reviewer validation before adoption.
